subject: Post-demo: Ephemeral data window & PII handling — proposed next steps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Kelly Martin <kelly.martin@orthosys.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Ephemeral data window & PII handling — proposed next steps

Kelly — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

- Ask summary from your side:
  - Primary requirement: no persistent user content storage (0-retention) for inference inputs/outputs.
  - Secondary: short-lived operational logs for troubleshooting/observability are acceptable if PII is redacted and retention is constrained to a narrow window.
  - Data residency: all processing must occur in a US region (prefer us-east-1).

- Redwood's proposed approach (initial):
  - Inference payloads: default ephemeral handling — not written to persistent disk; in-memory KV cache only.
  - Operational logs: redact PII at collection and retain aggregated traces/telemetry for 48 hours by default; we can propose a 24-hour window if that helps a security exception.
  - Optional: we can implement an account-scoped policy to zero out KV cache after request completion (effectively 0-retention for model context).

- Open items / ask of you:
  - Please confirm whether 24h vs 48h operational window is a hard requirement or guidance.
  - Can your security team accept redaction + short retention for logs vs. literal no-logging?
  - Any specific fields you consider PII that must be removed at collection (names, SSN, MRN, full DOB, etc.)? A short list will help us map redaction rules.

Attached: redwood-ephemeral-proposal-ORT-v1.pdf (high-level config + policy options).

If okay, next step I suggest is a quick call with your security contact and our privacy lead (cc'd laura and priyom here) to lock the retention window and redaction scope.

Thanks —
Sergio
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: Kelly Martin <kelly.martin@orthosys.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Ephemeral data window & PII handling — proposed next steps

Thanks Sergio — appreciate the concise recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- OrthoSys position: we are aiming for an effective 0-retention policy for clinical text (inference inputs/outputs) to meet our patient privacy commitments. However we recognize operational realities and may accept tightly scoped telemetry for platform health as long as: 
  1) Telemetry is redacted of direct identifiers before leaving compute nodes,
  2) Retention is capped at 24 hours, and
  3) Logs are stored in a customer-dedicated bucket with access controls (not mixed with other tenants).

- Our security team prefers the shortest window possible. 24 hours is our preference, 48 is a stretch. We will need a written description of the redaction approach and an architecture diagram showing where redaction happens across the data path.

- Attached is a short spreadsheet with our initial ask list (orthosys-security-ask-list.xlsx). Security will be available for a 30-minute sync next Tue (11/10) 10:30am ET.

Would you and laura/priyom be available?

Best,
Kelly

Forwarding Kelly's latest — they want 24h retention for telemetry + customer-dedicated storage and redaction before logs leave the node.

Immediate asks for legal/privacy/design: 
- Laura: can we commit to a 24-hour operational log window for a single-account carveout? We may flag this as an exception on the hosted plan (will require a ticketed route-to-market and additional compliance review).
- Priyom: security/engineering: can you outline where in the request path we can perform deterministic redaction of PII (edge ingress vs. pre-logging hook)? Also what impact does turning KV cache zero-out on every request have on latency and model quality for short-context experiences?

Notes: Kelly asked for an architecture diagram showing redaction location — I attached the proposal we sent them; please iterate and I'll pass back.

Thanks —
Sergio

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Kelly Martin <kelly.martin@orthosys.ai>, security@orthosys.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Post-demo: Ephemeral data window & PII handling — proposed next steps

Thanks — I sketched an initial technical position below (high level) we can present to Kelly/security next Tue: 

- Redaction placement: implement deterministic redaction in the ingress layer (API gateway) before any logs are emitted to the observability pipeline. This guarantees no direct PII leaves the compute node. We will maintain a configurable redaction rule set per account.

- Retention window: we can offer a documented policy for OrthoSys: 
  Option A (recommended): 24-hour operational window for raw traces + aggregated telemetry retained for 90 days. Raw traces will be held only in the customer-dedicated S3 bucket with strict IAM and auto-delete lifecycle (24h).
  Option B: 48-hour window if OrthoSys needs extra troubleshooting time (requires a signed retention exception).

- KV cache behavior: we can enable a per-account flag to zero out KV cache on request completion. This yields effectively 0-retention for model context but increases cold-start token generation in some flows. Practically: for short interactive sessions (<1 min) impact is negligible; for multi-turn sessions where history is desired we recommend scoped caching with explicit TTL (e.g., 30s–5min) and an audit.

- Data residency: redirect processing to us-east-1 for OrthoSys accounts; we will document region pinning in the Dedicated/Private offer or as a hosted account control (regional policy).

Next steps I propose for Tue 11/10 call (30 min):
1) Walk the redaction diagram (I'll bring the ingress flow).
2) Confirm 24h vs. 48h decision and whether they need a signed exception (legal).
3) Align on storage location (customer-dedicated bucket) and access rules.

I'll prepare a short slide with the diagram + the Option A/B language and a sample retention clause for legal to review. Sergio — if you can confirm the time with Kelly I'll lock it.

— Priyom
